outline: Scientific visualization is the use of computer graphics to visually represent the composite meaning of the large amount of data obtained by scientific computation, extensive monitoring, or engineering experiments. The scientific visualization in this semester focuses on finite element structural analysis data. Students are assumed to be familiar with stress and strain of materials, matrix/vector operations, and are capable of writing programs by using at least one type of programming language.
schedule:
Week 1: Introduction to Scientific Visualization and Finite Element Analysis
Week 2: Installation of Matlab and OpenSees
Week 3: Static stress/strain analysis of 3D framed structures
Week 4: 2D/3D coordinate transformation in stress/strain visualization
Week 5: Static stress/strain analysis of 3D shelled structures
Week 6: Stress/strain visualization of shell elements
Week 7: Modal analysis and visualization of 3D framed structures
Week 8: Dynamic stress/strain analysis and visualization
Week 9: Midterm
Week 10: Nonlinear response history analysis and visualization (1)
Week 11: Nonlinear response history analysis and visualization (2)
Week 12: Integration methods of nonlinear response history analysis
Week 13: Nonlinear algorithms of nonlinear response history analysis
Week 14: Presentations of proposals for final projects (1)
Week 15: Presentations of proposals for final projects (2)
Week 16: Advanced topics of scientific visualization (1)
Week 17: Advanced topics of scientific visualization (2)
Week 18: Final project presentations
assessment:
1. Lecture activities (attendance, interaction, lecture assistance) (20% +/- 5%)
2. Midterm (20% +/- 5%)
3: Final Presentation (20% +/- 5%)
4: Final Report (40% +/- 5%)
